title: Naturality comparison for the tensor–Hom and Verdier exchanges
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use its constructible finite-Tor categories and completed, rationalized, or common-stage operations, respectively. Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d$ over $k$, and assume either that $X$ is proper or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ (the hypotheses of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality]); let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $a:X\to s$ be its structure morphism, and let $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. Put $C=Ra_!K$, $\omega_s=R\mathrm{id}_s^!\Lambda_s$, $\mathbb D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_s)$, $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$ and $\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!\Lambda_s)$. Let $\nu:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ be the identity counit and put $c=Ra^!(\nu)$, whose isomorphism and counit compatibility are supplied at each of the four stages by [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport]. Let $b_{\omega}$ and $b_1$ denote the tensor–internal-Hom exchange isomorphisms [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] at $f=a$, $M=K$ and $N=\omega_s$, resp. $N=\Lambda_s$. Let $\eta_K=Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)\circ b_{\omega}^{-1}:\mathbb D_sC\to Ra_*\mathbb D_XK$ be the Verdier exchange map [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] at $f=a$, $M=K$. Then naturality in $N$ gives
$$b_1\circ Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)\circ b_{\omega},$$
so $\eta_K=b_1^{-1}\circ R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)$.

Let $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ be the point fibre, with the tensor and unit comparisons $t_{P,Q}:F(P\otimes^LQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}FP\otimes^L_\Lambda FQ$ and $u:F\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$ of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Let $\operatorname{ev}^{\omega}:C\otimes^L\mathbb D_sC\to\omega_s$ and $\operatorname{ev}^1:C\otimes^LH\to\Lambda_s$ be the internal-Hom evaluations and $\operatorname{ev}_\Lambda$ the coefficient evaluation. Let $\alpha_C:F\mathbb D_sC\to R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FC,\Lambda)$ be the coefficient tensor–Hom transpose of $u\circ F(\nu\circ\operatorname{ev}^{\omega})\circ t_{C,\mathbb D_sC}^{-1}$, and let $\alpha_C^1:FH\to R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FC,\Lambda)$ be the evaluation-preserving comparison of [lem-sf-identification-fibre-adjunction] at $P=C$, i.e. the transpose of $u\circ F(\operatorname{ev}^1)\circ t_{C,H}^{-1}$. Then
$$\alpha_C=\alpha_C^1\circ F R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu).$$
Consequently the composite $G=F(\eta_K)\circ\alpha_C^{-1}:R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FC,\Lambda)\to F Ra_*\mathbb D_XK$ (from which, followed by $FRa_*\mathbb D_XK=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$, the global-duality isomorphism of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] is constructed) satisfies
$$G=F(b_1^{-1})\circ(\alpha_C^1)^{-1}.$$ The displayed equations hold in the actual category at the chosen coefficient stage, with $b_{\omega}$ and $b_1$ the exchanges at that stage; their naturality in $N$ is the naturality asserted in [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom].

source.place: proof, Step 3: naturality of tensor–Hom in $N$, evaluation comparison, and identification with global duality

proof.text:
Fix one of the four coefficient realizations. The tensor--internal-Hom exchange of [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] is natural in its target variable N. Apply that naturality square to the morphism nu:omega_s -> Lambda_s. The exceptional inverse-image map in the square is Ra^!(nu), which is c by [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport]. Therefore the two paths from Ra_* RHom_X(K,Ra^! omega_s) to RHom_s(C,Lambda_s) agree, namely
$$b_1\circ Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)\circ b_{\omega}.$$
The coefficient-transport statement supplies the isomorphism and counit normalization at the selected stage, so this calculation applies equally to the completed, rationalized, and common-stage realizations.

source.place: proof, second sentence: the tensor–Hom chain at $N=\Lambda$ (naturality in $N$)

proof.text:
By the definition in the statement, $\eta_K=Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)\circ b_{\omega}^{-1}$ (the Verdier exchange composite named in the statement, whose second factor uses $c=Ra^!(
u)$ of [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport]). Compose the equation of Step 1 on the right with $b_{\omega}^{-1}$, and then on the left with $b_1^{-1}$. Associativity and the inverse identities give
$$\eta_K=b_1^{-1}\circ R\mathcal Hom_s(C,
u).$$
Sources and targets: $R\mathcal Hom_s(C,
u):\mathbb D_sC	o H$ and $b_1^{-1}:H	o Ra_*\mathbb D_XK$. This is a formal cancellation in the actual coefficient category at the fixed stage.

u\circ\operatorname{ev}^{\omega}$. (b) Naturality of $t$ in its second variable [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] gives $t_{C,H}^{-1}\circ(1_{FC}\otimes Fho)=F(1_C\otimesho)\circ t_{C,\mathbb D_sC}^{-1}$. (c) By the evaluation equation of $\alpha_C^1$ in [lem-sf-identification-fibre-adjunction],
$$\operatorname{ev}_\Lambda\circ igl(1_{FC}\otimes\alpha_C^1Fho igr)=u\circ F(\operatorname{ev}^1)\circ t_{C,H}^{-1}\circ(1_{FC}\otimes Fho)=u\circ F igl(\operatorname{ev}^1\circ(1_C\otimesho) igr)\circ t_{C,\mathbb D_sC}^{-1}=u\circ F(
u\circ\operatorname{ev}^{\omega})\circ t_{C,\mathbb D_sC}^{-1},$$
using (b) and then (a). The right side is the map whose coefficient tensor–Hom transpose is $\alpha_C$ by definition; since transposition is a bijection,
$$\alpha_C=\alpha_C^1\circ F R\mathcal Hom_s(C,

The same computation holds at the integral stage in the completed point category and at the two field realizations in their rationalized or common-stage form, because $t$, $u$ and the evaluation equation are stated at each of these stages in the two cited nodes.

source.place: proof, second sentence: 'the adjoint of $\beta_K$ is the composite of the duality isomorphism ...' (point evaluation comparison)

proof.text:
By the definition in the statement, $G=F(\eta_K)\circ\alpha_C^{-1}$. Substitute the formula for $\eta_K$ from Step 2 and the comparison identity from Step 3 (all maps are isomorphisms: $b_1$ by [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom], $\rho=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)$ since $\nu$ is an isomorphism, hence $\alpha_C^1$ and $\alpha_C$ together):
$$F(\eta_K)\circ\alpha_C^{-1}=F(b_1^{-1})\circ F\rho\circ(F\rho)^{-1}\circ(\alpha_C^1)^{-1}.$$
The middle factors cancel, giving
$$G=F(b_1^{-1})\circ(\alpha_C^1)^{-1}.$$
This $G$ is the composite through which [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] is built (its construction composes $F(\eta_K)$ with the inverse of the evaluation transpose $\alpha_C$ and with the global-section identification); the step uses only the definitions in the statement. All maps are the specified maps at the chosen coefficient stage.

split_report.summary: Split the naturality calculation into four steps: target-variable naturality of the tensor--Hom exchange, formal cancellation identifying the Verdier exchange, evaluation-preserving point-fibre naturality, and substitution into the global-duality construction. No new nodes were needed; all non-elementary inputs are existing statements.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the second sentence of the blueprint proof of sk-thm-sf-identification (the tensor–Hom chain at N=Lambda identified with the duality isomorphism): Step 1 naturality in N, Step 2 Verdier exchange, Step 3 point evaluation comparison, Step 4 comparison with the global-duality composite. (Maintainer-reader fix: the earlier place 'Step 3: ...' named a step label of the parent DAG node, not a paragraph of the blueprint file.)

tool_uses.why: Uses the stated natural tensor and unit comparisons of the point fibre to transport the evaluation-preserving internal-Hom comparison; the identification-exchange route has no separate node supplying this generic monoidal fibre fact.
